message.content:
Let  
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}19&30\\-45&-71\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its trace and determinant are
\[
\operatorname{tr}A=19-71=-52,\qquad \det A=19(-71)-30(-45)=1.
\]
Thus the characteristic polynomial of \(A\) is
\[
\lambda^2+52\lambda+1=0,
\]
so its eigenvalues are
\[
\lambda=-26\pm 15\sqrt3.
\]

If \(M^3=A\), then \(M\) commutes with \(A\), so its eigenvalues are the real cube roots of the eigenvalues of \(A\). Now
\[
(-2+\sqrt3)^3=-26+15\sqrt3,\qquad (-2-\sqrt3)^3=-26-15\sqrt3.
\]
Hence the eigenvalues of \(M\) are \(-2\pm\sqrt3\).

For eigenvalue \(\lambda=-26\pm15\sqrt3\), the corresponding cube root \(\mu=-2\pm\sqrt3\) satisfies
\[
\mu=\frac{\lambda-4}{15}.
\]
Therefore
\[
M=\frac{A-4I}{15}.
\]
Now
\[
A-4I=\begin{pmatrix}15&30\\-45&-75\end{pmatrix},
\]
so
\[
M=\frac1{15}\begin{pmatrix}15&30\\-45&-75\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\-3&-5\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Indeed,
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\-3&-5\end{pmatrix}^3
=
\begin{pmatrix}19&30\\-45&-71\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\-3&-5\end{pmatrix}}\).
